     3	description: Generate professional PDF/HTML reports with charts, tables, and narrative from data. Supports templates, branding, and automated report generation.

     5	
     6	# Report Generator
     7	
     8	Create professional, data-driven reports with charts, tables, and narrative text. Perfect for business reports, analytics dashboards, status updates, and automated reporting pipelines.
     9	
    10	## Quick Start
    11	
    12	```python
    13	from scripts.report_gen import ReportGenerator
    14	
    15	# Create a simple report
    16	report = ReportGenerator("Monthly Sales Report")
    17	report.add_text("This report summarizes sales performance for Q4 2024.")
    18	report.add_table(sales_data, title="Sales by Region")
    19	report.add_chart(sales_data, chart_type="bar", title="Revenue by Month")
    20	report.add_text("Key findings: Revenue increased 25% quarter-over-quarter.")
    21	report.generate().save("sales_report.pdf")
    22	
    23	# From template
    24	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("executive_summary")
    25	report.set_data(data_dict)
    26	report.generate().save("exec_summary.pdf")
    27	```
    28	
    29	## Features
    30	
    31	- **Multiple Output Formats**: PDF, HTML
    32	- **Rich Content**: Text, tables, charts, images, headers
    33	- **Chart Types**: Bar, line, pie, scatter, area, heatmap
    34	- **Table Formatting**: Auto-styling, conditional formatting
    35	- **Templates**: Pre-built report templates
    36	- **Branding**: Logo, colors, fonts, headers/footers
    37	- **Sections**: Table of contents, page numbers, appendices
    38	- **Data Integration**: CSV, DataFrame, dict inputs
    39	
    40	## API Reference
    41	
    42	### Initialization
    43	
    44	```python
    45	# New report
    46	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title")
    47	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title", subtitle="Q4 2024 Analysis")
    48	
    49	# From template
    50	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("quarterly_review")
    51	
    52	# With config
    53	report = ReportGenerator("Title", config={
    54	    "page_size": "letter",
    55	    "orientation": "portrait",
    56	    "margins": {"top": 1, "bottom": 1, "left": 0.75, "right": 0.75}
    57	})
    58	```
    59	
    60	### Report Metadata
    61	
    62	```python
    63	# Title and subtitle
    64	report.set_title("Annual Report 2024")
    65	report.set_subtitle("Financial Performance Analysis")
    66	
    67	# Author and date
    68	report.set_author("Analytics Team")
    69	report.set_date("December 2024")
    70	report.set_date_auto()  # Use today
    71	
    72	# Organization
    73	report.set_organization("Acme Corporation")
    74	report.set_logo("logo.png")
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Adding Content
    78	
    79	#### Text Content
    80	
    81	```python
    82	# Simple paragraph
    83	report.add_text("This is a paragraph of analysis text.")
    84	
    85	# Styled text
    86	report.add_text("Important finding!", style="highlight")
    87	report.add_text("Key metric: 42%", style="metric")
    88	
    89	# Headers
    90	report.add_heading("Executive Summary", level=1)
    91	report.add_heading("Revenue Analysis", level=2)
    92	report.add_heading("By Region", level=3)
    93	
    94	# Bullet points
    95	report.add_bullets([
    96	    "Revenue increased 25% YoY",
    97	    "Customer acquisition up 15%",
    98	    "Churn rate decreased to 3%"
    99	])
   100	
   101	# Numbered list
   102	report.add_numbered_list([
   103	    "Expand to European markets",
   104	    "Launch mobile application",
   105	    "Implement AI-driven analytics"
   106	])
   107	```
   108	
   109	#### Tables
   110	
   111	```python
   112	# From DataFrame
   113	import pandas as pd
   114	df = pd.DataFrame({
   115	    'Region': ['North', 'South', 'East', 'West'],
   116	    'Revenue': [100000, 85000, 92000, 78000],
   117	    'Growth': ['12%', '8%', '15%', '5%']
   118	})
   119	report.add_table(df, title="Regional Performance")
   120	
   121	# From dict/list
   122	data = [
   123	    {'Product': 'A', 'Sales': 1000, 'Profit': 200},
   124	    {'Product': 'B', 'Sales': 1500, 'Profit': 350}
   125	]
   126	report.add_table(data, title="Product Summary")
   127	
   128	# With styling
   129	report.add_table(df, title="Sales Data",
   130	    highlight_max=['Revenue'],       # Highlight max values
   131	    highlight_min=['Growth'],        # Highlight min values
   132	    currency_cols=['Revenue'],       # Format as currency
   133	    percent_cols=['Growth'],         # Format as percent
   134	    align={'Region': 'left', 'Revenue': 'right'}
   135	)
   136	```
   137	
   138	#### Charts
   139	
   140	```python
   141	# Bar chart
   142	report.add_chart(
   143	    data=df,
   144	    chart_type="bar",
   145	    x="Region",
   146	    y="Revenue",
   147	    title="Revenue by Region"
   148	)
   149	
   150	# Line chart
   151	report.add_chart(
   152	    data=time_series_df,
   153	    chart_type="line",
   154	    x="Month",
   155	    y=["Sales", "Forecast"],
   156	    title="Sales Trend"
   157	)
   158	
   159	# Pie chart
   160	report.add_chart(
   161	    data=category_df,
   162	    chart_type="pie",
   163	    values="Amount",
   164	    labels="Category",
   165	    title="Budget Allocation"
   166	)
   167	
   168	# Chart options
   169	report.add_chart(
   170	    data=df,
   171	    chart_type="bar",
   172	    x="Region",
   173	    y="Revenue",
   174	    title="Revenue Analysis",
   175	    color="#3498db",
   176	    width=6,           # inches
   177	    height=4,
   178	    show_values=True,
   179	    show_legend=True
   180	)
   181	```
   182	
   183	#### Images
   184	
   185	```python
   186	# Add image
   187	report.add_image("screenshot.png", caption="Dashboard View")
   188	report.add_image("diagram.png", width=5, caption="Architecture Diagram")
   189	```
   190	
   191	#### Special Elements
   192	
   193	```python
   194	# Page break
   195	report.add_page_break()
   196	
   197	# Horizontal line
   198	report.add_divider()
   199	
   200	# Spacer
   201	report.add_spacer(height=0.5)  # inches
   202	
   203	# Callout box
   204	report.add_callout(
   205	    "Key Insight: Customer retention improved 20% after implementing the new onboarding flow.",
   206	    style="info"  # info, warning, success, error
   207	)
   208	
   209	# Quote
   210	report.add_quote(
   211	    "Data is the new oil.",
   212	    attribution="Clive Humby"
   213	)
   214	```
   215	
   216	### Sections and Structure
   217	
   218	```python
   219	# Start a new section
   220	report.start_section("Financial Analysis")
   221	
   222	# Add content to section
   223	report.add_text("...")
   224	report.add_table(...)
   225	
   226	# End section
   227	report.end_section()
   228	
   229	# Table of contents (auto-generated)
   230	report.enable_toc()
   231	
   232	# Appendix
   233	report.start_appendix()
   234	report.add_heading("Raw Data", level=2)
   235	report.add_table(raw_data)
   236	```
   237	
   238	### Branding and Styling
   239	
   240	```python
   241	# Logo and organization
   242	report.set_logo("logo.png", width=150)
   243	report.set_organization("Acme Corp")
   244	
   245	# Colors
   246	report.set_colors(
   247	    primary="#1e40af",      # Headers, accents
   248	    secondary="#6b7280",    # Secondary text
   249	    background="#ffffff"    # Background
   250	)
   251	
   252	# Fonts
   253	report.set_fonts(
   254	    heading="Helvetica-Bold",
   255	    body="Helvetica"
   256	)
   257	
   258	# Header and footer
   259	report.set_header("Confidential - Internal Use Only")
   260	report.set_footer("Page {page} of {total}")
   261	
   262	# Watermark
   263	report.set_watermark("DRAFT")

   266	### Templates
   267	
   268	```python

   270	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("executive_summary")
   271	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("quarterly_review")
   272	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("project_status")

   286	
   287	### Generation and Export
   288	
   289	```python
   290	# Generate report
   291	report.generate()
   292	
   293	# Save as PDF
   294	report.save("report.pdf")

   296	# Save as HTML

   304	## Templates

   334	## CLI Usage
   335	
   336	```bash

   346	
   347	### CLI Arguments
   348	
   349	| Argument | Description | Default |
   350	|----------|-------------|---------|
   351	| `--config` | Report configuration JSON | - |
   352	| `--template` | Template name | - |
   353	| `--data` | Data JSON file | - |

1	# Global Fuel Price Trends (1970–2026)
     2	
     3	## About the Dataset
     4	
     5	This dataset, sourced from Kaggle (minahilfatima12328/global-fuel-price-trends-19702026), provides a monthly time series of crude oil prices spanning from January 1970 through 2026. It is designed to support historical analysis, data visualization, and trend identification in the global energy sector. The dataset is particularly useful for researchers, data science learners, and analysts investigating long-term fuel price dynamics shaped by geopolitical events, global demand shifts, and macroeconomic conditions.
     6	
     7	- **File**: `fuel_prices_1970_2026.csv`
     8	- **Total Rows**: 675
     9	- **Total Columns**: 2
    10	- **Granularity**: Monthly observations
    11	- **Time Span**: Approximately January 1970 to mid-2026
    12	
    13	## Column Schema
    14	
    15	| Column Name | Type | Description |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| `Date` | String | The date of the observation in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Each entry represents the first day of a given month (e.g., `1970-01-01` represents January 1970). This column serves as the time axis for the entire dataset. |
    18	| `Crude_Oil_Price` | Float | The crude oil price for the corresponding month, expressed in US dollars per barrel (USD/bbl). This is the primary metric of the dataset and reflects the global benchmark price of crude oil. |
    19	
    20	## Key Column Details
    21	
    22	### Date
    23	The `Date` column is stored as a string and follows the ISO 8601 date format (`YYYY-MM-DD`). All dates correspond to the first day of each month, providing a consistent monthly cadence. With 675 rows, the dataset covers approximately 56 years of monthly data. Analysts should parse this column into a proper datetime type for time series operations such as resampling, rolling calculations, and period-based grouping.
    24	
    25	### Crude_Oil_Price
    26	The `Crude_Oil_Price` column contains the monthly crude oil price in US dollars. Early values in the dataset (e.g., $1.21 in January 1970) reflect the historically low and stable prices of the pre-oil-crisis era. Over the decades, prices have experienced dramatic swings — from the oil embargoes of the 1970s, the price collapse of the mid-1980s, the spike preceding the 2008 financial crisis, the shale revolution of the 2010s, the COVID-19 demand shock in 2020, and subsequent recovery. The dataset may include projected or estimated values for the most recent months approaching 2026.
    27	
    28	## Data Quality Notes
    29	
    30	- **Missing Values**: Based on the row count of 675 for a dataset spanning roughly 56 years (which would yield approximately 672 monthly observations), the data appears largely complete. However, analysts should verify whether any months contain null or anomalous values in the `Crude_Oil_Price` column.
    31	- **String Date Column**: The `Date` column is stored as a string rather than a native date type. It must be converted to a datetime format before performing any time-based analysis.
    32	- **Forward-Looking Data**: Since the dataset title indicates coverage through 2026, some of the later data points may represent forecasts or projections rather than actual observed prices. Analysts should note this distinction when interpreting recent values.
    33	- **Single Variable**: The dataset contains only one numeric variable (crude oil price). All analysis dimensions (yearly trends, decade groupings, volatility windows) must be derived from the `Date` column through feature engineering.
    34	- **Currency**: Prices are assumed to be in nominal US dollars. No inflation adjustment is provided in the raw data; analysts may wish to apply CPI-based deflation for real-price comparisons across decades.
    35	
    36	## Suggested Use
    37	
    38	This dataset is well-suited for time series trend analysis, volatility studies, decade-based comparative analysis, and historical event correlation. Its simplicity (two columns) makes it accessible for learners while still offering rich analytical depth across more than five decades of global energy pricing history.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('benchmark/data.csv')
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'])
df = df.sort_values('Date').reset_index(drop=True)

# Basic info
print('Rows:', len(df))
print('Date range:', df['Date'].min(), 'to', df['Date'].max())
print('Missing prices:', df['Crude_Oil_Price'].isna().sum())

# KPIs
prices = df['Crude_Oil_Price']
min_price = prices.min()
max_price = prices.max()
min_date = df.loc[prices.idxmin(), 'Date']
max_date = df.loc[prices.idxmax(), 'Date']
price_range = max_price - min_price

# CAGR
start_price = prices.iloc[0]
end_price = prices.iloc[-1]
years = (df['Date'].iloc[-1] - df['Date'].iloc[0]).days / 365.25
cagr = (end_price / start_price) ** (1/years) - 1

# Std dev
std_dev = prices.std()

# Max MoM change
df['MoM_abs'] = df['Crude_Oil_Price'].diff().abs()
df['MoM_pct'] = df['Crude_Oil_Price'].pct_change().abs() * 100
max_mom_abs_idx = df['MoM_abs'].idxmax()
max_mom_pct_idx = df['MoM_pct'].idxmax()

# Max YoY change
df['YoY_abs'] = df['Crude_Oil_Price'].diff(12).abs()
df['YoY_pct'] = df['Crude_Oil_Price'].pct_change(12).abs() * 100
max_yoy_abs_idx = df['YoY_abs'].idxmax()
max_yoy_pct_idx = df['YoY_pct'].idxmax()

print('\n=== KPIs ===')
print(f'Price Range: \${min_price:.2f} ({min_date.strftime(\"%Y-%m\")}) to \${max_price:.2f} ({max_date.strftime(\"%Y-%m\")}) = \${price_range:.2f}')
print(f'CAGR: {cagr*100:.2f}%')

The 2020s data (through March 2026) reveal a market still processing the dual shocks of COVID-19 demand destruction and the 2022 supply reconfiguration. Key observations from the recent trajectory:

  • COVID Collapse & Rebound: Prices fell from $61.63 (Jan 2020) to $21.04 (Apr 2020), a –65.9% drop in three months. The recovery to $48.73 by December 2020 was equally rapid, reflecting unprecedented fiscal and monetary stimulus.
  • 2022 Geopolitical Spike: The Russia-Ukraine conflict pushed prices to $116.80 in June 2022 — the highest level since 2008 — before retreating as supply realigned and demand growth moderated.

  2. Demand cycles drive duration; supply shocks drive magnitude. The 2003–2008 super-cycle was demand-led and multi-year; the 2020 collapse was demand-led and abrupt.
  3. Nominal prices have structural upside bias. Even after accounting for inflation, the long-term nominal CAGR and the recurring emergence of new highs suggest that "lower for longer" periods (1986–1999, 2015–2016, 2020) are temporary features, not terminal states.
